title: Monthly statements and monthly totals don't reconcile
statement:
Our reconciliation job runs two checks for every account and every month of 2024:

  (a) statement(txs, account, 2024, m).closing == statement(txs, account, 2024, m + 1).opening
  (b) statement(txs, account, 2024, m).credits + .debits == monthly_totals(txs, 2024, account)[m]

Both checks fail on real data. The failures cluster around month ends and on accounts from our Chicago office, whose exports carry -05:00 / -06:00 offsets (e.g. 2024-03-31T21:30:00-05:00). Totals for the year also don't match the sum of the individual transactions we expect in 2024.

The reporting policy is written at the top of ledgerlite/dates.py: every reporting period is a UTC calendar month treated as a half-open interval [first instant of the month, first instant of the next month); timestamps with an offset are placed by their UTC instant; naive timestamps are UTC. Make statements and monthly totals follow that policy.
targetSkill: timezone- and boundary-correct period logic across modules
